business_problem: Founded in 2026, Belgian company Inku relies entirely on Google Cloud to operate "Brand Engine", an AI layer that understands enterprise brands intimately and enables them to produce content at scale while maintaining total control over their image.
solution_summary: "The idea is to stop starting from a blank prompt, but rather from a system that already understands the brand," notes Gus Vanherf. "By injecting context from the information stored on our platform into the generation pipelines, we enable our clients to produce content that is not just fast to create, but above all consistent with their brand, accurate, and ready to use." Designed to manage the entire end-to-end process from the initial brief to asset production the platform offers a unified environment where teams no longer just generate content: they orchestrate complete campaigns faster and with an unprecedented level of control. To realize this vision, Inku built a sophisticated architecture entirely running on Google Cloud. business_outcome: A Belgian company founded in 2026, aims to transform brand content creation by making it more consistent, faster, and easier to industrialize. Designed to meet the exploding visual needs of marketing teams, its platform relies on an AI trained on each brand's unique DNA, ensuring content is always faithful to its identity.
metrics: Campaign creation costs reduced by 70% to 75%
Where creation costs once rapidly accumulated, the platform drives reductions of 70% to 75%, allowing companies to reallocate those budgets toward more strategic investments.
Global teams can build briefing, create campaign assets, comment and edit with the team, approve and ship in a matter of minutes, not months.
This enables companies to move from brief to campaign in just a few days, delivering significant gains in costs, speed, and quality.
